scope: Independently reproduced preexisting CP12 publication failure, also present in CP22. This is separate from parse-cache changes and does not invalidate preserved timing observations.

finding.mechanism: Temporary is created before OpenOptions(create_new).open. If the temporary path already exists, create_new returns AlreadyExists without ownership, but Temporary::drop removes that preexisting path.
finding.observable_effect: A requested executable at frontend-cp12-v1/.pending-<compiler PID>-0 is removed after native publication even though the request reports Success and fresh Verify=1. The .ll sidecar remains.
finding.minimal_fix: Construct the temporary path first, open with create_new, then arm the guard only after success. Keep cleanup armed for every later error/cancellation and disarm only after successful rename.
required_controls: Preexisting temporary-path sentinel and native executable survive AlreadyExists unchanged.
Owned temporary files are cleaned on post-create write/flush/rename/cancellation failures; the original final entry survives.
Successful publication leaves a readable reusable cache entry and no owned temporary file.

reproduction.mechanism: CP12 Temporary is armed before create_new succeeds. Existing published output causes AlreadyExists and Drop removes the unowned existing path.

limits: Release binary source identity is the existing frozen baseline build record plus rechecked exact binary SHA256, not a new independent release rebuild.
This probe is an intentional deterministic output/temp collision in a reviewer-created directory; it does not model an adversarial cache writer.
CP26 initially authorizes only parse_cache.rs. CP12 needs its own authorized write scope and exact-commit review.
